item.title: Gemini Live is Google Home's next upgrade project, yet only subscribers can enjoy it
item.dc:content:
Google's smart home ecosystem continues to evolve, and it looks like Gemini is preparing for a speech upgrade. What's more, Nest devices are in for an update designed for the colder months ahead.

In a Google Home community post, the company teased what's coming next for its home AI, Gemini. A "faster, more natural" Gemini Live experience is reportedly "coming soon" to Google's smart home devices. The post explains it is preparing to enhance the AI's "speech-to-speech architecture" to achieve this snappier upgrade. However, this comes with an additional "Hey Gemini, let's chat" prompt.

With this, homeowners can do everything from quick, simple requests to full-on brainstorming sessions with Gemini Live. This experience might mirror what you'd find on your Android phone. Users can reportedly plan trips, organize dinner plans, and "interrupt Gemini naturally," and it seems to keep pace. Google says these enhanced Gemini Live sessions can continue "without stepping out of the chat."

It can also control your connected smart devices, set timers, and more.

While it sounds convenient, all of this will be tucked behind the Google Home Premium subscription plan. Google says users will need its Standard or Advanced plan to experience Gemini Live's updates on speakers and displays.

Elsewhere, Google's Nest devices are preparing for a December update (via 9to5Google). The Nest Thermostat will soon tell users how much money it has saved them while managing their home. Additionally, Google is expanding its Home support to third-party thermostat sensors from IKEA, Eve, and Aqara. These will reportedly connect to your 4th-gen Nest Learning Thermostat only once this arrives next month.

The home still needs fixing

Google Home has a ton of features and updates, but it hasn't been flawless. The ecosystem has had its fair share of issues, and a recent update was busy squashing bugs. Users recently discovered that Live View was busted for their older Nest doorbells, which also affected Arlo cams. A follow-up update fixed those issues. Another issue, where some cams would reboot on their own, was fixed, too.

Those fixes came with an expansion of Gemini's "voice management." Gemini now covers "thermostats, fans, air purifiers, robot vacuums, EV chargers, and smoke detectors." In a separate case, Gemini was suffering from a strange "Sorry, I didn't understand" bug. Even stranger: this problem would happen when users hadn't said anything. This problem has been fixed, along with an issue where timers/alarms didn't make sound, causing some people to miss them.

item.title: These are the 12 best Android accessories I've tested and couldn't live without
item.dc:content:
Once you have one of the best Android phones, or maybe you're hanging onto an older device, you'll want to get the most out of it. You can enhance the experience with accessories, and these run the gamut from earbuds (check out our related guide) to protective cases, power banks, and more.

The first item I always get for a new phone is a fitted case, and there's one that's almost my first buy. From there, I'll eventually switch the case to something more stylish, bolder, or whatever fits my needs. But having a solid starter case is essential.

Another essential I won't go without is a power bank, and I can't count how many I have. I'm still on the hunt for the perfect one, but there are a few awesome ones I love.

There's lots more you can get to complement your phone, whether it's to charge it quickly or on the go, mount it to a surface, enhance fitness, take better photos, provide solid grip, and more.

We're here to help with some recommendations for fantastic and affordable Android phone accessories. We've used many of these ourselves and can confirm they are worth the money.

The 12 best Android phone accessories

Dual-function phone holder
Scosche
MagicMount Flask

I have been using this water bottle for a few years now, and I can't say enough good things about it. Not only is it a fantastic water bottle that keeps my water cold all day as I guzzle and sip, but it also has a neat flip-up spout that prevents spills. It's connected to a built-in straw that comes out easily for cleaning. On the bottom is a removable rubber piece that provides both grip on a flat surface and can function as a dog bowl for water.

OK, wait, what does this have to do with tech? At the top is a circular MagSafe holder to accommodate your MagSafe-enabled phone, like the Google Pixel 11 Pro, or a phone with a MagSafe case. I use it daily to mount my phone to take post-workout selfies to share with my workout group. It's also handy at the gym so you don't have to rest your phone on the floor while you try to beat your bench press record. It's also handy at the beach, in the park, and even in the car to hold the phone neatly while you drive.

Coolest (literally) power bank
Anker
MagGo 2 Pro Power Bank

Anker is one of the best brands when it comes to portable power banks, and this one, just launched at IFA Berlin in September 2026, has a built-in fan to ensure it's kept cool while charging all your high-powered devices. The 10,000mAh power bank has a 45W USB-C port and Qi2 surface for wireless charging at the fastest possible speed.

The handy screen on the side provides charging status and can even detect what device you plug in. The bottom fan keeps it running below 96.8°F at all times, so while it charges your phone at a speedy pace, it's kept cool the entire time. The kickstand is a nice touch, too, so you can prop your phone up while on a video call or watching a movie on the plane and charging it at the same time.

Personal health coach
Google Fitbit
Air

For under $100, you can get a handy bracelet that tracks everything from your activity and workouts to sleep and even vitals like heart rate, blood oxygen, and stress. The Fitbit Air is comfortable and affordable, and the Google Health app is full of useful analysis to help you keep on top of your health and wellness.

You can sign up for Google Health Premium for $9.99/mo. ($99.99/yr.) for access to the AI Coach, deeper analysis, personalized workout plans, and more. But it comes with a three-month trial so you can try it out first and decide after that. I ranked the Fitbit Air as the best screenless tracker you can buy, and our Fitbit Air reviewer deems it to be "forgettable in the best possible way." In other words, all you need to do is wear it, charge it weekly, and check in on the app whenever you want or if you get a pertinent notification to enjoy a distraction-free health monitoring experience.

You can never have enough
UGREEN
USB-C to USB-C Cable 100W - 2-pack

It doesn't matter how many USB-C cables I have lying around the house; they never seem to be enough. Just an hour ago, my 14-year-old asked me for an extra-long one he could take to school to charge up his Chromebook when it's running low (because, of course, he forgets to charge it at home all the time).

UGREEN is a great brand and this two-pack support 100W power for fast-charging of compatible devices (with a compatible power brick) and are 6.6 feet long, so great for classrooms, running behind your home office desk, reaching from one end of the couch to the other, or setting up in a hotel where the outlet is always in the most inconvenient possible spot. The braided housing provides durability, while a smart chip detects what it plugs into to avoid overcharging. With two in a pack, you can keep one at home and the other in your carry-on.

Essential travel accessory
Anker
Universal Travel Charger

I travel quite a bit, and a multi-outlet power brick is one of the items I keep in my carry-on. This allows me to plug in all my gadgets, like my phone, smartwatch charger, headphones, portable camera, and more to one outlet. But what about an international charger? I have a separate brick with European plugs that I have used on a few trips over the last few years. This convenient accessory is the only one you'll need.

The 100 GaN charger has built-in prongs that work in tons of countries, and you can swap among them as needed. Push out the AC plugs in the U.S., then pull them back in and use the EU plugs in Germany. It's ultra-compact and lightweight, and once plugged into a wall outlet, you can power up to three USB-C and one USB-A device. It's such a clever concept that it's worth the slight markup compared to others, since you're essentially getting a travel multitool for charging.

Show off your phone
Casetify
Clear Case for Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra

A protective case can be stylish, but if you want to show off the bold, bright, or elegant finish of the phone you bought, you'll want to consider a clear case. Casetify is one of my favorite phone case brands, and this one, shown here for the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra (and available in other designs), is so simple yet gets the job done.

Let the beauty of the phone itself shine through by adding protection with 6.6-foot drop protection. It's Qi2 charging compatible and optimized to prevent yellowing over time. Why bother spending so much time choosing the right phone color only to cover it anyway, after all?

Never lose your gear
Google
Pixel Tag

Google has finally entered the item tracker space, and its Google Pixel Tag is slim, lightweight, and durable, with a replaceable CR2032 battery that lasts up to a year. Pair it with your Android phone, attach it to a valuable item, like your keys, or place it in your wallet, purse, or luggage, then track its location using Google Find Hub and its network of users around the world. Plus, you can also use the Tag itself to ring your phone if you can't find it.

It's a great gift item you can buy in multi-packs as well, ideal for students, forgetful parents or spouses, maybe even for travel, pets, and other peace of mind. I have one in the zippered pocket of my belt bag, which will help me keep track of its location should I ever misplace it or accidentally leave it behind somewhere. After having one such bag stolen, this could be the difference between getting back your lost item or not.

Samsung
60W Charging Block

Did you know the latest Samsung phones don't come with charging bricks in the box? You can use any charging brick or plug directly into a USB-A or USB-C outlet. But if you want to maximize charging speeds for a Galaxy or other phone that supports faster charging, consider this 60W charging block.

The set includes two single USB-C outlet chargers so you can keep one in your home office and one at the remote office. Simple and affordable, it will get your devices charged up in no time, so you can go about your day. And the price is right.

Your makeshift home studio
Anxre
71-inch Phone Tripod

Whether it's for recording home videos for social content or to bring with you, this tripod is convenient and collapsible. The holder is expandable to fit phones from 4 up to 7 inches in size and it has a 1/4-inch screw mount for connecting other devices. It expands up to 71 inches for taller vantage points, like dancing videos and interviews. Then, collapse it to 13.5 inches and take it on the go as a selfie stick.

It comes with a remote shutter, too, so you can handle solo content for your burgeoning TikTok channel or Instagram Reels. You can adjust and lock it in various height positions so it can meet all your video needs. It's a good gift for a budding content creator.

A good first case
Spigen
Tough Armor Case for Pixel 11 Pro

Whenever I get a new phone, this is always the first case I get for it. It's simple, offers good protection, and even has a recessed flip-out kickstand for propping the phone upright in portrait or landscape mode.

Available in three finishes for the Google Pixel 11 Pro (you can find this case for virtually any phone imaginable), it's compatible with Google PixelSnap and MagSafe cases. Get three layers of protection with PC, TPU, and an inner cushion. It has raised edges to protect the camera lenses and screen and meets military-grade drop protection. For this price, it's a great backup case or a simple one when you just want affordable but effective protection.

Pocketable charging
INIU
Mini Portable Charger

This portable charger is so adorably cute, yet it boasts a 10,000mAh battery and supports 45W fast charging on the go. It's so small that it can fit in your pocket. It has a detachable, nylon-braided USB-C cable lanyard so you don't even need to bring a separate cable with you.

TempGuard 2.0 ensures safe charging with no overheating, even for more demanding devices, like your Nintendo Switch 2. Get it in one of six colors; it makes a perfect stocking stuffer item.

Look your best
Altson
60 LED Portable Selfie Light

Look your best for Zoom or Google Meet calls, social media videos, virtual interviews, and more with this neat accessory. The light clips to your phone (or laptop, monitor, or camera) to help provide softer, more flattering light for your skin tones. It's lightweight and compact, so you can bring it with you.

There are three light modes, including white, natural, and warm, with color temperature from 2500-6500K and 10 lighting brightness modes to suit every scenario. It even rotates 160° to capture different angles. It runs for 4-15 hours per charge, depending on the brightness level, and comes with a hot shoe mount for tripods, cameras, selfie sticks, and other accessories. This is a gift that keeps on giving for content creators.

When we tested the Google Home Speaker, the listening experience offered more than satisfactory audio quality because of the device's spherical design. Unlike previous Google speakers, its latest inductee optimizes audio output so that it reaches every corner of a room.

On top of its technical smarts, its woven fabric look gives it a smart yet pretty look, which would look good on any bookcase or coffee table!

item.dc:content:
The new Googlebook laptops might be all that people in the Android space are talking about right now when it comes to portable computing, but that doesn't mean Chromebooks have gone away.

In fact, you can currently find them at great prices, like this powerful Chromebook Plus from Lenovo on sale for just $349 at Best Buy thanks to a crisp $50 discount.

As this is a Chromebook Plus model, you're getting better performance than your average Chromebook and a host of additional features. This specific model, the Lenovo Chromebook Plus i, boasts an Intel Core 3 Processor N355, 8GB of RAM, and 128GB of storage, which is more than enough for day-to-day usage and productivity tasks.

It's got a large 15.3-inch 1920x1200 screen, with the 16:10 aspect ratio making it easy to multitask and view multiple windows at the same time.

Chromebook Plus i 15.3": was $399 now $349
This Intel Core 3-powered Chromebook Plus has 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage. It's a good pick for day-to-day use or productivity tasks and has some Gemini-powered AI features built in.View Deal

Before the arrival of Googlebooks, Chromebooks were Google's big foray into the laptop market. They run ChromeOS, a lightweight operating system designed to work well with the Android ecosystem. While the most common Chromebooks have developed a bit of a reputation for being cheap and low-spec, the Chromebook Plus line is different.

It's more premium, with minimum spec requirements that ensure a smooth experience in a range of tasks. They have modern processors and at least 8GB of RAM, a full HD IPS display (or higher resolution), and a high-quality webcam. There are also some exclusive software differences, and namely, some handy AI-related features. They have integrated Gemini, for example, with easy access to image generation.

They're great if you're looking for a reliable workhorse that you can pick up without breaking the bank.

item.title: I’ve been using Sony’s WH-1000 XM5 headphones for four years, and I’ve never looked back — here’s why I’d recommend them this Black Friday
item.dc:content:
About four years ago, I was anointed with a pair of what were the best wireless headphones at the time, and all this time later, my Sony WH-1000 XM5s are still going strong, and I've never looked back.

Now that we're creeping even closer to Black Friday season, I cannot stress enough how perfect an opportunity you have to get one at a discounted rate. As it stands, the best Black Friday 2026 deal I've come across is at Best Buy, where Sony's WH-1000 XM5 headphones are now $299.99 down from $398.

And yes, Black Friday is still a week away, but stock is much higher during early sales, and if you're not one to wait for the possibility that a better deal will arise, it's best to act sooner rather than later.

WH-1000 XM5 Headphones: was $398 now $229.99
Compared to its listing price at the time of release, a sub-$250 offer on some of the best headphones I've used isn't terrible at all. While it's still not exactly a budget-friendly option, the newer XM6 model is still on the pricier side even during early Black Friday sales. View Deal

If you're an audio novice and the price tag still scares you, allow me to reassure you.

As a beginner, you may think that a cheaper pair of headphones with standard audio features will be enough to get you by. And yes, there are plenty of budget-friendly alternatives with above-average performance, but I was also a newbie, and I can confidently say that introducing yourself to audio tech through a brand like Sony will go such a long way.

Sure, $229.99 is still a lot of money even when it's a deal, but once you take the plunge, you won't have to spend this money for a good few years before the headphones start to show signs of wear and tear. I'm four years in, and the audio output is still as punchy and bold as it was when I first purchased them.

Speaking of audio, the Sony WH-1000 XM5 headphones pack a versatile listening experience, bringing out the very best of lossless and hi-res music streaming. Its Active Noise Cancellation succeeds at drowning out pretty much everything around you, making them perfect for noisy commutes. At the same time, the Ambient Sound setting is useful for letting in outside noise while you listen to music, which you can easily enable and disable via the button on the left ear pad.

If there's anything to note, it would be the lack of collapsible ear pads, which are a fan-favorite feature from models past (it just makes it a lot easier for travelling). The Platinum Silver version is also prone to discoloring, so Black is probably the better shade to opt for, but other than that, they've presented zero disappointments.

item.title: This gigantic Bluetooth speaker is my go-to for room-shaking sound — and it could be a Black Friday favorite thanks to a massive price cut
item.dc:content:
You don't have to sacrifice sound quality if you're after a speaker that can get seriously loud. Case in point: the JBL Boombox 4. This portable Bluetooth boombox is an absolute beast, reaching around 104 dB at full volume, which is roughly as loud as a motorcycle. This makes it perfect for parties and social events, where it delivers true home-filling sound.

It's a great pick at full price, but right now Best Buy has knocked $150 off to bring it down to just $399.95. It's well worth the investment, as it's a highly versatile speaker. With an IP68 waterproof and dustproof rating and an extremely durable rubber and cloth exterior, you can take it outside in any conditions. Poolside cocktails? It's got you covered. Rainy BBQ? Handled with no sweat.

Featuring two large, powerful woofers, two tweeters, and three passive radiators, the audio quality is formidable, offering both punchy bass and a surprising level of depth and clarity. I like to use mine while I work (it's actually playing right now as I write this), and find that the 1/3 volume mark is where it really shines – delivering beautiful sound that comfortably fills my large room without becoming too overwhelming.

Battery life is good too. JBL says that you can get about 28 hours from each charge, though you should expect something around the 10-hour mark unless you're playing music very quietly. This model features a user-replaceable battery as well, so you don't need to worry about your expensive purchase becoming unusable due to cell degradation in five or ten years.

This absolute audio behemoth is my go-to Bluetooth speaker when I want something loud that still sounds superb. It delivers thumping bass while remaining beautifully clear, and is practically designed with waterproofing and a useful built-in carrying handle.View Deal

✅Recommended if: You want a durable, portable Bluetooth speaker that offers incredible volume without sacrificing sound quality. It's ideal for social events, but is also a brilliant pick for at-home listening. Just make sure your phone volume isn't set too high, or the neighbours might complain!

❌Skip this deal if: You would rather go for an even more portable model. The JBL Boombox 4 is designed to be moved around, but it's still quite large and heavy, making it difficult to move over long distances despite the carrying handle.

If you want a portable speaker to take on your next hike or holiday retreat, then I would instead consider the brand's smaller models like the JBL Flip 7 or JBL Grip. They don't sound as good and are nowhere near as loud, but they are simply more practical in those kinds of situations.

item.title: No console? No problem — how to play titles like GTA 6 on your phone
item.dc:content:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is just hours away, and while console owners are looking forward to diving into the huge virtual world of Vice City, I'm sure that there are plenty of mobile players feeling left out.

After all, GTA 6 is currently the highest-rated game of all time on review aggregator Metacritic, with early reviews calling it a once-in-a-generation experience that you surely won't want to miss.

If you primarily game on a phone or tablet, unfortunately you're out of luck when it comes to playing GTA 6 on the go unless you already have access to a compatible cosnole – but there are plenty of Android native alternatives worth checking out instead.

Remote play is an option, but only if you own a console

If you want to play GTA 6 on your phone and happen to own a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X or Xbox Series S and a digital copy of the game, then remote play is an option. Both ecosystems let you stream the game from your console to your phone in order to play it in different rooms at home or, if the internet allows, when you're out and about.

If you own a PlayStation 5, then you'll need to download the PS Remote Play app and go through the on-screen process to link it to your console. There's no dedicated app for Xbox, and you instead need to visit the dedicated remote play website to get everything set up.

A compatible controller is recommended for the best experience, and you can use the one that came with your console or pick up a spare below.

Wireless Controller: was $64.99 now $49.49
This no-nonsense gamepad is fully compatible with Xbox Remote Play and easy to hook up to your mobile phone so a perfect choice for GTA 6. Just prop your phone up using a makeshift stand, and you can dive right in.View Deal

For PS Remote Play, there's no better option than the official DualSense Wireless Controller. It's easy to pair and packed with unique features.View Deal

If you don't have access to the required hardware then you're not totally out of luck, read on for some other options.

There are plenty of native Android GTA ports

In my view, the best alternative is to pick up one of the many native ports of older Grand Theft Auto titles available on the Google Play Store. The best part is that they don't cost anything to try out.

GTA: Vice City - Definitive is an official remastered version of the 2002 installment Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. Set in the 1980s, it takes place in the same city as GTA 6 and offers its own unique storyline and a more condensed open world to explore. Yes, it's obviously not as technologically advanced as the new game (there has been more than two decades between them, after all) – but it's still a timeless classic and could be just the thing to tide you over until the FOMO wears off.

That initial free download nets you a 30-minute free trial, which you can then upgrade into the full game with a one-time in-app fee if you are enjoying the experience.

You can do the same with GTA III - Definitive, which is a remaster for the third game in the series. GTA: San Andreas - Definitive is also available, though this entry costs money up front to play.

All three games have full touch control support, so you won't need to buy a separate controller either.

PC emulation could let you play the previous entry first

If you would rather play a more modern Grand Theft Auto game, then PC emulation is worth looking into.

You're going to need a seriously beefy phone for this, however, and I would recommend going with a dedicated gaming model like the RedMagic 10 Pro or the newly released RedMagic 11 Pro for the best performance.

These phones come with a built-in PC game emulator, which lets you download games you own from Steam with ease. If you own Grand Theft Auto 5 on Steam, you can get it running smoothly on your phone at around 720p resolution after fiddling with the graphics settings.

This lets you experience the whole previous entry, which is the next best thing to GTA 6.

You can even do this on any high-end mobile device by seeking out and downloading a compatible PC game emulator, but the setup process is much more complicated, and I wouldn't recommend it for beginners or those not willing to tinker with their tech.

Lastly, you can't forget the mobile alternatives

If you're just after a game like the Grand Theft Auto series, then there are some native Android titles that offer similar gameplay.

I've been testing OneState Social RP over the last week or so, which is a free-to-play life role-playing game set in modern Los Angeles.

It takes a bit of time to get going, but it's a surprisingly expansive experience that lets you pursue different career paths and engage in online multiplayer activities. You can become a police officer, for example, or join a criminal gang while working to earn money that you can spend buying homes, cars, and more.

It's all based around big servers filled with hundreds of other players, who you're encouraged to interact and role-play with. It's like having a whole virtual world on your phone!

Retro City Rampage DX is also a great experience. It's only a few bucks to buy and offers top-down open-world action that's very reminiscent of the early GTA games. It's wacky, filled with fun challenges, and features more than 60 story missions to complete.

Finally, the popular free-to-play open-world RPG NTE: Neverness to Everness should be on your radar. It has slick anime graphics with an incredibly detailed and massive open-world city. The setting is more fantastical than the other two games that I've been talking about, but I personally enjoy the tense, supernatural tone of its main plot.

If you primarily game on a phone or tablet, unfortunately you're out of luck when it comes to playing GTA 6 on the go unless you already have access to a compatible cosnole – but there are plenty of Android native alternatives worth checking out instead.

Remote play is an option, but only if you own a console

If you want to play GTA 6 on your phone and happen to own a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X or Xbox Series S and a digital copy of the game, then remote play is an option. Both ecosystems let you stream the game from your console to your phone in order to play it in different rooms at home or, if the internet allows, when you're out and about.

If you own a PlayStation 5, then you'll need to download the PS Remote Play app and go through the on-screen process to link it to your console. There's no dedicated app for Xbox, and you instead need to visit the dedicated remote play website to get everything set up.

A compatible controller is recommended for the best experience, and you can use the one that came with your console or pick up a spare below.

Wireless Controller: was $64.99 now $49.49
This no-nonsense gamepad is fully compatible with Xbox Remote Play and easy to hook up to your mobile phone so a perfect choice for GTA 6. Just prop your phone up using a makeshift stand, and you can dive right in.View Deal

For PS Remote Play, there's no better option than the official DualSense Wireless Controller. It's easy to pair and packed with unique features.View Deal

If you don't have access to the required hardware then you're not totally out of luck, read on for some other options.

There are plenty of native Android GTA ports

In my view, the best alternative is to pick up one of the many native ports of older Grand Theft Auto titles available on the Google Play Store. The best part is that they don't cost anything to try out.

GTA: Vice City - Definitive is an official remastered version of the 2002 installment Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. Set in the 1980s, it takes place in the same city as GTA 6 and offers its own unique storyline and a more condensed open world to explore. Yes, it's obviously not as technologically advanced as the new game (there has been more than two decades between them, after all) – but it's still a timeless classic and could be just the thing to tide you over until the FOMO wears off.

That initial free download nets you a 30-minute free trial, which you can then upgrade into the full game with a one-time in-app fee if you are enjoying the experience.

You can do the same with GTA III - Definitive, which is a remaster for the third game in the series. GTA: San Andreas - Definitive is also available, though this entry costs money up front to play.

All three games have full touch control support, so you won't need to buy a separate controller either.

PC emulation could let you play the previous entry first

If you would rather play a more modern Grand Theft Auto game, then PC emulation is worth looking into.

You're going to need a seriously beefy phone for this, however, and I would recommend going with a dedicated gaming model like the RedMagic 10 Pro or the newly released RedMagic 11 Pro for the best performance.

These phones come with a built-in PC game emulator, which lets you download games you own from Steam with ease. If you own Grand Theft Auto 5 on Steam, you can get it running smoothly on your phone at around 720p resolution after fiddling with the graphics settings.

This lets you experience the whole previous entry, which is the next best thing to GTA 6.

You can even do this on any high-end mobile device by seeking out and downloading a compatible PC game emulator, but the setup process is much more complicated, and I wouldn't recommend it for beginners or those not willing to tinker with their tech.

Lastly, you can't forget the mobile alternatives

If you're just after a game like the Grand Theft Auto series, then there are some native Android titles that offer similar gameplay.

I've been testing OneState Social RP over the last week or so, which is a free-to-play life role-playing game set in modern Los Angeles.

It takes a bit of time to get going, but it's a surprisingly expansive experience that lets you pursue different career paths and engage in online multiplayer activities. You can become a police officer, for example, or join a criminal gang while working to earn money that you can spend buying homes, cars, and more.

It's all based around big servers filled with hundreds of other players, who you're encouraged to interact and role-play with. It's like having a whole virtual world on your phone!

Retro City Rampage DX is also a great experience. It's only a few bucks to buy and offers top-down open-world action that's very reminiscent of the early GTA games. It's wacky, filled with fun challenges, and features more than 60 story missions to complete.

Finally, the popular free-to-play open-world RPG NTE: Neverness to Everness should be on your radar. It has slick anime graphics with an incredibly detailed and massive open-world city. The setting is more fantastical than the other two games that I've been talking about, but I personally enjoy the tense, supernatural tone of its main plot.

item.title: Google just made its best Gemini agent free — here's where you can get it
item.dc:content:
Google is giving millions of people access to Gemini's Tasks feature for free.

The tool can run multi-step requests in the background, and Google is expanding its capabilities to include shopping, phone calls, email, and deeper integrations into its apps.

Formerly known as Spark, Tasks is now rolling out to free Gemini users in the US, Japan, South Korea, Canada, Australia, and India, as per Josh Woodward, VP of Product for AI at Google. This agentic mode previously required a paid AI Pro or AI Ultra tier.

It runs on Google’s new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model and allows users to switch from Chat to Task mode to pass off work instead of babysitting every step. That could involve asking Gemini to plan a trip, research a topic, set up a morning briefing, or manage recurring tasks while you’re busy doing literally anything else.

Gemini is moving closer to a real personal assistant

Google is also launching a range of new capabilities, initially available in the US. It can call local businesses with Google Duplex, make purchases with Google Pay, receive text messages with RCS, and accept forwarded emails with Gmail. It can also log into websites using Google Password Manager without ever exposing passwords outside of Google’s ecosystem.

To test it, flip the toggle above your mobile prompt box (or below on the web) from "Chat" to "Task." You can even bypass the app entirely by forwarding emails or texting Gemini directly through Google Messages and iMessage.

The Workspace integration is also receiving a major upgrade. Google says Gemini can now more reliably draft or send emails, create and edit Google Docs and Sheets, and add multiple events to Google Calendar without toggling between apps.

There is still a catch

As you can imagine, having an AI in your inbox, passwords, and payment methods does raise some security concerns. Google says when browsing the web, Tasks runs inside an isolated virtual machine, protected against prompt injection and Google Safe Browsing protections. Gemini also asks for confirmation before it buys anything and can ask for clarification if your instructions aren’t clear.

That said, Google still has some work to do. Some sites might prevent Gemini from completing a task and ask you to step in and finish the last step. For now, the promise of a digital assistant that can really take work off your hands is getting closer — but still isn’t quite ready to be trusted with everything.

item.title: Bringing it back? Samsung's 'variable aperture' could return on these Galaxy S phones
item.dc:content:
Rumors are back about an old theory about Samsung's current-gen phones. Some claim the company is seriously considering bringing back an older aperture feature for future cameras.

These rumors resurfaced after tipster Yogesh Brar suggested a classic return could grace Samsung's next Galaxy S phones in a couple of years. Brar claims Samsung is considering bringing variable aperture back to its Galaxy S flagship phones (via GSMArena). However, if true, consumers shouldn't expect this on every phone.

Brar says Samsung might explore this only with the Galaxy S28 Pro and S28 Ultra. If this is anything to go by, perhaps we should expect the Pro to stick around. Recent rumors suggest the alleged Galaxy S27 Pro will feel like an Ultra, but be positioned between it and the Plus (despite its supposed specs).

The tipster also suggests that Samsung "isn't the only brand exploring VA for their flagship device."

Would Samsung only bring this back for the sake of competition?

Nickolas Diaz

These rumors have come and gone

We're going to walk back through history. In late 2025, rumors surfaced that Samsung was considering bringing back variable aperture on its Galaxy S phones. These rumors claimed the Korean OEM was doing so to better contend with Apple's upcoming 2025 iPhones: the iPhone 18 and 18 Pro Max. Samsung hasn't had variable aperture since the Galaxy S9 days. It was a feature that covered narrow and wide apertures to help users take photos in a range of situations.

Several months later, rumors said variable aperture was headed to the Galaxy S26 series (which didn't happen). However, reports said Samsung was working with its Electro-Mechanics and MCNEX teams on the required tech. This would've enabled "true" variable aperture, letting the camera lens easily shift between apertures. It wouldn't have been digital, like the Galaxy S25 Ultra.

If we can expect this in two years, how limited would it be? Remember: the Galaxy S9 and even the S10 had variable aperture, but it was restricted to shifting between f/1.5 and f/2.4. Truthfully, that's not good enough for above-average output.

item.title: Samsung One UI 9.5 beta released for Galaxy S26: Here's what's new [Changelog]
item.dc:content:
Samsung has officially released the One UI 9.5 beta for Galaxy S26 users.

After weeks of testing and rumors, Samsung has officially announced the One UI 9.5 beta for Galaxy S26 users. According to the company's announcement, the beta will give users an early look at One UI 9.5 ahead of its stable release. We expect the stable version of One UI 9.5 to arrive alongside the Galaxy S27 series launch next year, but until then, the beta will give users a taste of what's coming.

It's worth noting that the One UI 9.5 beta is currently available only for the Galaxy S26 series, and that too in select markets, including Germany, India, Korea, Poland, the UK, and the US. Similar to previous beta programs, users will have to sign up through the Samsung Members app to get access.

As for what's new, Samsung says One UI 9.5 introduces updated camera controls that give users more flexibility and creative control when taking photos and videos. According to the company, enhanced Pro and Pro Video modes offer customizable controls and presets for different shooting conditions.

There's also a new Mindful Note feature that allows users to express their feelings and journal their thoughts, similar to what's already available through Apple's Journal app and Google's Pixel Journal.

Alongside this, Samsung is introducing a new medication tracking feature that allows users to add prescriptions, vitamins, and supplements, set customized reminders, and keep track of their medications directly from their phones.

Probably the best feature Samsung has introduced with One UI 9.5 is the ability to lock individual apps. Until now, users had to rely on Secure Folder to keep apps behind biometric authentication. But Samsung is finally giving users more flexibility with App Lock.

The company says users will be able to keep individual apps private by locking them behind biometric authentication or their screen lock. Samsung also says that when an app is locked, its notification content and widgets will be hidden as well.

In addition to this, One UI 9.5 introduces a dedicated floating shortcut button that gives users quick access to frequently used controls. There are also improved hearing aid controls, allowing users to adjust the volume directly from the notification panel.

For now, Samsung has started rolling out the One UI 9.5 beta to Galaxy S26 users in select countries. You'll need to enroll through the Samsung Members app to try it out. However, if you'd rather wait for the stable update, you'll likely have to wait another couple of months until the Galaxy S27 series launches next year.

One UI 9.5 changelog

Tipster Ice Universe has also shared the One UI 9.5 changelog on X. Here's everything new in the first build of One UI 9.5:

1. Camera

1.1 Simplified Camera Controls

- A cleaner interface makes camera settings easier to access and compare without excessive scrolling. The bottom control area has been redesigned for more convenient operation.

1.2 Enhanced Pro Mode and Pro Video

- Improved shutter speed and frame rate controls.

- More precise shutter speed adjustments.

- A redesigned audio control interface in Pro Video mode.

2. Lock Screen Customization

2.1 Live Effects for the Lock Screen

- Add dynamic depth effects to your lock screen.

- Elements in the wallpaper move at different speeds when the device is tilted, creating a sense of depth.

2.2 More Clock Display Options

- Choose from 10-second, 30-second, 1-minute, 5-minute, and 10-minute time intervals.

- Customize these settings through the clock options in the upper-right corner of the lock screen editor.

2.3 Expanded Now Bar Animations

More Now Bar animations are available across different scenarios.

- Enjoy dynamic visual effects for supported sports events, including team scores and victories.

3. Digital Wellbeing

3.1 App Opening Delay

- Set a waiting period of up to 10 seconds before selected apps open.

- Designed to reduce impulsive app usage and encourage more mindful screen time.

4. Security and Privacy

4.1 App Lock

- Protect individual apps using a PIN, pattern, password, or biometric authentication.

- Keep sensitive app content secure when sharing your device.

4.2 Enhanced Privacy Display (Supported Models)

- Privacy Display can activate automatically when entering a PIN, pattern, or password.

- Additional support for private Gallery albums and locked Samsung Notes.

- Automatic activation options for selected apps and notifications.

4.3 Improved Biometric Authentication

- Enhanced facial recognition and fingerprint authentication.

- Support for authentication flows involving both biometric methods.

- Fingerprint authentication can be completed directly on the sensor without an additional on-screen confirmation.

4.4 Redesigned Biometric Enrollment

- Fingerprint and facial recognition setup screens feature a cleaner interface and refined animations.

5. My Files

5.1 Built-in Office Document Preview

- Preview DOCX and PPTX files directly in My Files without installing Microsoft Office.

- PPTX slideshow playback is also supported.

5.2 Improved Storage Management

- Easier selection and deletion of uncategorized files and files currently in use when managing storage.

6. Samsung DeX

6.1 Improved Maximized Window Experience

- Maximized windows can occupy more screen space.

- Refined status bar and taskbar layouts provide a more immersive desktop experience.

6.2 Expanded Snap Layouts

- More window snapping options beyond traditional split-screen layouts.

- Arrange two, three, or four applications on the screen simultaneously.

7. Samsung Health

7.1 Sleep Coaching Improvements

- Start sleep coaching using sleep data collected over the previous two to three days.

- Get personalized recommendations based on sleep patterns and goals.

7.2 Mood Tracking and Journaling

- Record emotions, thoughts, and personal reflections.

- Journal entries can be linked to mood records for easier tracking.

7.3 Improved Medication Management

- Manage registered medications more conveniently through Samsung Health.

- Expanded medication management functionality.

7.4 Customizable Health Cards

- Rearrange health cards such as Activity, Sleep, Body Composition, Mood, and Food Tracking.

- Prioritize the information you use most frequently.

8. Accessibility

8.1 Floating Accessibility Shortcut

- A dedicated floating button provides quick access to accessibility features.

- Improved positioning and transparency controls.

8.2 Enhanced Hearing Aid Controls

- Adjust the volume of connected hearing aids.

- Choose which sounds to hear, including ambient audio, speech, and notifications.

9. Additional Improvements

9.1 Faster Settings Search

- Search for settings and features more efficiently.

- Recently searched items are displayed for quicker access.

9.2 Downloadable Galaxy Wallpapers

- Download classic Over the Horizon wallpapers from previous Galaxy generations.

- Set your favorite wallpapers directly on your device.

10. Other Changes

10.1 Discontinued Audio Features

- Audio Broadcast and Enhanced Audio Services are no longer supported starting with One UI 9.5.

item.title: Samsung's Galaxy Buds 3 Pro just got a massive 47% price cut ahead of Black Friday
item.dc:content:
Black Friday is almost upon us, and if you're looking to snag a great deal ahead of the main event without spending too much on a pair of premium wireless earbuds, Samsung's Galaxy Buds 3 Pro are worth checking out.

They're currently down to just $100 on Amazon, a massive 47% discount from their usual $190 price. In fact, this is the lowest price we've seen for Samsung's flagship earbuds yet, making them an even more tempting buy ahead of Black Friday.

Samsung's Galaxy Buds 3 Pro are down to just $100 on Amazon, a massive 47% discount from their usual $190 price. These premium wireless earbuds offer excellent sound quality, adaptive ANC, wireless charging, and up to 26 hours of battery life with the case.View Deal

  • 20+ Black Friday 2026 deals for Android lovers

✅ Recommended if: You own a Samsung Galaxy phone, want premium wireless earbuds with ANC and excellent sound quality, or are looking for flagship features without spending more than $100.

❌ Skip this deal if: You use an iPhone, want the longest possible battery life, or prefer earbuds that offer the same features regardless of which Android phone you use.

Samsung may have newer earbuds in its lineup now, but the Galaxy Buds 3 Pro are still a fantastic pair of wireless earbuds, especially if you're using a Samsung Galaxy phone. They offer pretty much everything you'd expect from premium earbuds, including great ANC, excellent sound quality, wireless charging, and plenty of Galaxy AI features that make them worth it even today.

Samsung moved away from its bean-shaped earbuds design to a stem-style design with the Galaxy Buds 3 Pro, and many people who've used these earbuds have praised their fit and comfort. That's also partly why the ANC works so well, as a good seal helps block out more background noise.

But one of the biggest reasons to get these earbuds is that they pack pretty much everything you'd expect from a flagship pair without the flagship price tag. They originally launched for around $250, and even though they're no longer the latest model, they're still among the best wireless earbuds you can get right now.

Battery life is pretty decent as well. Samsung claims up to six hours of listening with ANC enabled, or up to 26 hours with the charging case. You also get an IP57 rating for the earbuds, which is a nice bonus if you plan to use them during workouts or while traveling.

Of course, you'll get the most out of these earbuds if you own a Samsung Galaxy phone. Galaxy AI features and Samsung's higher-quality audio codec work best with a Galaxy phone. That said, you can still use the earbuds with other Android phones, though some features won't be available.

On the whole, if you've been waiting for a good deal on a pair of premium wireless earbuds, I wouldn't overlook these. At their usual $190 price, there are plenty of alternatives worth considering, but at just $100, you're getting flagship-level features for almost half the price.

item.title: Not so fast—some Moto Signature 27 users will have to deal with a smaller battery
item.dc:content:
Motorola went all-in on premium this year with the Signature 27. While many consumers eagerly awaited this phone, some won't see it at its full potential.

Certain specs must be met before companies (or rather, consumers) can slap a premium label on a phone. The Motorola Signature 27 focuses on key areas: its display, camera, chipset, and battery. It's the latter—its battery—that's come under scrutiny in one market. According to Android Authority, the Motorola Signature 27's battery will suffer a hit overseas.

Reports have conflicted with the Signature 27's original 7,000mAh battery announcement. The publication highlighted this, then reached out to Motorola for clarification. A spokesperson responded, stating the device "will feature a different battery configuration in Germany." As a result, it looks like German consumers will find the Signature 27 with a 5,500mAh cell, not 7,000mAh.

This is a sharp 1,500mAh drop, but Motorola says it had no choice.

In its statement, Motorola told the publication that it had to drop the phone's battery to "comply with local regulatory requirements related to lithium batteries." The report adds that this huge battery cut is worth roughly 17 hours of battery time (~61 hours vs 77 hours).

Taking a hit

Strangely, a report claimed U.K. consumers might've suffered from this battery cut, too. Apparently, the Signature 27 was listed with a 5,500mAh battery; however, it's reportedly since been updated to the higher figure.

It's unclear how this might affect German consumers who were interested in the Signature 27. The battery (right now) is the only aspect of the phone that's suffering from country-specific regulations. During launch, the phone was announced with an incredibly bright 6.8-inch Extreme AMOLED Duo display with 12,000 nits. Motorola stuck to its premium promise and delivered Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 SoC (a first for the brand).

For mobile gamers, the company integrated its ArcticMesh cooling system, increasing its size by 40% to help keep temperatures lower during longer sessions.

Android Central's Take

Would something like this matter to you? A reduction from 7,000mAh to 5,500 mAh, I mean.

Here's why I ask—and I'll play both sides here. Motorola wanted to release a phone that firmly leaned into "premium." One could say it did. However, if you look at Samsung and its Galaxy S26 Ultra (S25 Ultra... S24 Ultra...), it features a 5,000mAh battery. The Korean OEM has kept this exact same 5,000mAh cell for a while, and yet it's still premium. Premium tag, premium price, everything. Of course, Motorola's sharp reduction will cut down how long users can keep scrolling, but it's still more than Samsung's latest Ultra.

Ongoing discussion

item.title: Best of 2026: Google Play celebrates the year's top winners from Arknights: Endfield to thriller stories
item.dc:content:
It's that time of year again when the cold air mixes with a year's worth of new apps, games, and books. Google Play is celebrating its 2026 "Best Of" winners; see if your favorites won.

This morning (Nov. 17), Google announced its Best of Play award winners. As you'd expect, a few AI apps have made their way into the Best of 2026 celebrations. Google states a few winners highlight "a deeper need for technology that’s both highly efficient and genuinely supportive." The awards kick off with Best Overall Game and App. For the latter, Notability: AI & PDF Notes snags the top trophy for Best App, delivering a digital notebook experience for learning, work, and productivity.

Gamers, whether they're on PC or mobile, will recognize the Best Overall Game winner: Arknights: Endfield. Developed by GRYPHLINE, Arknights: Endfield offers a story-rich experience and an extensive factory-building function for gathering resources and crafting important supplies to level up characters, weapons, and more.

Google emphasized the need for technology to keep progressing and better accommodate users. That sentiment takes us into the next category: Best Cross-device Game and App.

For Best Cross-device App, Google named Strava: Run, Bike, Walk as the winner. We've tested and experimented with Strava for a while at Android Central. We've even visited its San Francisco HQ in 2025 and interviewed its CEO, Mike Martin, and Chief of Staff, Shelby Rhodes, about Athlete Intelligence. Strava also recently partnered with Google's Gemini to bring new insights through Connected Apps.

For Best Cross-device Game, Moonlight Peaks took the trophy. It's described as a slower, slice-of-life game where players often tend their magical crop garden or "woo werewolves."

Let's not forget all of the books that have come out this year. For fiction, Google awarded The Everlasting by Alix E. Harrow the "Favorite Fantasy" award and Anatomy of an Alibi by Ashley Elston the "Favorite Thriller" award.

Best Games of 2026

  • Best Multiplayer: Warframe
  • Best Pick-up and Play: Subway Surfers City
  • Best Indie: Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor
  • Best Story: Sea of Stars
  • Best Ongoing: Zenless Zone Zero

Best Apps of 2026

  • Best for Entertainment: Qobuz: Music & Editorial
  • Best Innovative App: Wispr Flow: AI Voice-to-Text
  • Best for Sports Fans: Sofascore: Live Sports Scores
  • Best for Creative Expression: ibis Paint X
  • Best for Kids and Families: Superfonik: Kids Learn to Read

You can view the full list of Best of 2026 winners for games, apps, and books. All winners here are from U.S. interactions (downloads, etc.). Similarly, Google highlighted the winners of its 2026 awards across Asia. While Arknights: Endfield secured the top spot for overall game, NTE: Neverness to Everness won the Best Cross-device game award.

LINE Music took the "Best for Entertainment" award based on Japanese users.

item.title: 25+ Black Friday 2026 deals for Android lovers — Samsung Galaxy, Pixel, Chromebooks and more
item.dc:content:
Black Friday deals season is already upon us. Feels like it comes around earlier each year, huh?

The Best Black Friday Deals For Android Fans

Get ready to smash that piggy bank and load up on savings, because it’s already looking like a particularly good year for Android fans.

We’re already seeing big retailers like Amazon, Walmart and Best Buy offering up early ‘holiday’ sales deals across a huge range of items — and for the Android native, that includes price slashes on flagship smartphones, Chromebooks, top audio gear, and mobile data plans.

From the latest Samsung foldables to half-price unlimited data, we’re pulling together the best offers we’ve seen across the web before the big Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales kick off officially on Friday 27 November and Monday 30 November respectively.

Hit that bookmark button and dive in — we’ll be updating this post regularly as the deals land to help you turn those pennies into pixels.

QUICK LINKS TO THE BIG BLACK FRIDAY SALES

  • Amazon: Big savings on tech essentials
  • Best Buy: Half price TVs, laptops, gadgets and more
  • Walmart: Members get early access to giant savings
  • Target: Great for pre-Christmas gifting prep
  • T-Mobile: Free premium handsets — including Samsung Galaxy — with select plans
  • Samsung: Up to $1,000 off 2026 flagship devices
  • Mint Mobile: Half price unlimited data with top Google Pixel devices

Today's best deals — Android Phones

Google Pixel 11 Pro XL (256GB): was $1299 now $794
A perfect pairing of device and data plan, Mint Mobile is not only offering a chunky saving on Google's Pixel 11 Pro XL handset, but it's also offering half-price unlimited data plans too. That's $180 bucks for a full year. You'll have to be a new customer to take advantage though. This one's the 256GB model, but the 512GB model is up for sale with the same data deal, too.View Deal

Google Pixel 11 Pro XL (512GB): was $1419 now $914
Here's that Mint Mobile Google Pixel 11 Pro XL handset deal again, but this time for the beefier 512GB storage size. Again, if you're a new Mint Mobile customer, you can also pair it with an unlimited data plan at half the usual cost — $180 dollars for a whole year. A great combo package.View Deal

Google Pixel 11 (256GB): was $899 now $399
If you can't stretch to the price of the big-screen top-tier XL Pro edition of this year's Pixel, there's a cracking deal on the standard Google Pixel 11, knocking a whopping $500 off the Android 17, 6.3-inch handset. Like the other Mint Mobile deals on offer this Black Friday, it too is on offer alongside a half-price unlimited data deal, bagging you all the GBs you can eat for $180 for a year. This deal right here is for the 256GB model, but the 512GB model also got a price cut via Mint.View Deal

Google Pixel 11 (512GB): was $1019 now $519
If you need a chunk more storage in your device, that Google Pixel 11 deal from Mint Mobile is also on the 512GB model, saving you $500 off the usual asking price. You can pair it with a year's worth of unlimited data from Mint Mobile too for just $180 — half what it'd normally set you back.View Deal

Samsung Galaxy S26 (512GB): was $1200 now $700
There's a chunky $500 to be saved on the Samsung Galaxy S26 at Mint Mobile this Black Friday, with the retailer putting the 512GB model of Samsung's 6.3-incher up for sale for just $700. Mint Mobile is also offering a nifty deal of half-priced unlimited data plans for new customers, getting you all the GBs you can handle for just $180 for the first year.View Deal

Nothing Phone (3) (256GB): was $699 now $499
If you're tired of cookie-cutter clone phones, it's about time you give Nothing and its unique Glyph Interface a try. Amazon is selling the Nothing Phone (3) at $499 for Black Friday — $200 off it's usual price. It's a slightly older model as a 2025 release, but there's still nothing (lolz) on the market that really looks like it, and it's Snapdragon 8s Gen4 chipset still gets the job done.View Deal

Nothing Phone (3) (512GB): was $799 now $599
If the Nothing Phone (3)'s angular industrial design and Glyph Interface has caught your eye, Amazon's also offering up the larger 512GB model with that same $200 saving. It's up for sale at $599 — a good price unlocked for a unique-looking handset.View Deal

Samsung Galaxy S26 FE: was $699.99 now $549.99
The Galaxy S26 FE is the most affordable entry in Samsung's Galaxy S26 line-up and offers something of a middle ground between flagship and budget options. It's thin and light, with a 6.7-inch display and the powerful Exynos 2500 chipset – plus comes with seven years of OS upgrades which is a real standout at this price.View Deal

Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8: was $1199.99 now $999.99
Samsung is letting you save up to $400 on the cutest foldable of the summer at its official store when you trade in your old device (or a still quite hefty $200 off without a trade-in). The Z Flip8 comes in a range of cool colors and fits wonderfully in a pocket or handbag thanks to its compact folded shape.View Deal

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8: was $1899.99 now $1549.99
The Galaxy Z Fold is one of the trendiest phones of 2026, with its distinct passport-size form factor making it a real head-turner. It's got a 7.6-inch folding screen (and a 5.5-inch front panel), with other major specs including 12GB of RAM and the flagship Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy processor. Perfect if you want something a little different from the usual foldable fare.View Deal

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra: was $2099.99 now $1749.99
The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is a super-powered version of the Z Fold 8 and Samsung's highest-end foldable right now. It's got a larger 8-inch inner screen and a 6.5-inch front display, making for easy multitasking, a better 200MP camera sensor, and a slightly larger battery capacity thanks to its increased size. View Deal

We called the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra's Privacy Display feature an "amazing achievement" in our review, and now it can be yours at a meaty saving thanks to this Black Friday offer. You get great performance, excellent AI features, and seven years of software updates here. The S Pen stylus is also built-in.View Deal

Wearable deals

Calling all lovers of the great outdoors, Samsung's robust Galaxy Watch Ultra2 takes everything you love about fitness tracking and times it by 10. We loved the flagship Running Coach feature, which provides solid assistance with training you for lengthy distances, while Trail Running modes provide turn-by-turn navigation for added accuracy. While it could do better battery-wise, it still makes a great outdoor companion and all-round fitness tracker — especially if you're looking for intricate features such as blood pressure monitoring.View Deal

If you're sticking to a budget this Black Friday, this early offer on the Google Pixel Watch 5 is one to add to your list — and it's one of our favorites. On top of its battery life (which matches the Galaxy Watch Ultra2), Google's most recent Pixel wearable is a joy to use for accurate distance and step tracking, and it even matched the Garmin Cirqa when gathering heart rate data across a plethora of workouts.View Deal

Audio deals

WH-1000 XM6 Wireless Headphones: was $459.99 now $398
With the WH-1000 XM6 headphones, Sony somehow managed to top the already-great XM5s. They pack even better ANC performance, a battery life to last you long work sessions or journeys, but the best part is the return of the folding ear pads. Users begged for the comeback, and Sony listened. Though it's not the biggest saving and you may be more lucky waiting until Black Friday itself, this is an opportunity to snatch a pair now at a small discounted price if you're impatient buyer.View Deal

Arc Ultra Soundbar: was $1099 now $849
If you're ready to take your home theater audio to the next level, this is the one to look out for. Out of all of our best soundbars, we still stand by the Sonos Arc Ultra as the one with the best smarts. its Dolby Atmos support makes a great fit for your existing setup, pairing nicely with larger TVs. It's still on the pricier side even with its Black Friday discount, but it's already beaten last season's price tag. View Deal

Solo 4 Wireless Headphones: was $199.95 now $129.95
If you're an audio novice looking for a solid entry-level pair of headphones, look no further. As well as Bluetooth connectivity, the Beats Solo 4 supports both USB-C and 3.5mm wired connections, which we recommend if you really want to enhance the audio from hi-res streaming platforms. For a sub-$150 set of over-ear headphones, you're getting more than enough features to get you by, but if ANC is non-negotiable, it may be better to seek alternatives. View Deal

Headphones (a): was $199 now $107
Nothing's Black Friday discounts have already started, and for a model that was released just this year, it's not a terrible deal at all. Although we haven't had the opportunity to test them out yet, we do know that they offer a generous 135 hours of playback with ANC switched off, with support for Hi-Res Audio Wireless with the LDAC codec to optimize high-quality music streaming. Features aside, Nothing has one of the strongest audio brand identities, so there's no denying that the headphones look good. View Deal

Beam Gen 2: was $499 now $399
Unlike its Ultra Arc sibling, this model is built for smaller TVs and certainly smaller budgets. It's compact in size, but despite this, it doesn't compromise on the features, boosting seamless connectivity with other speakers in the Sonos family. It also doubles as a smart speaker, which removes the need to purchase an Amazon or Google speaker on top. View Deal

QuietComfort Ultra: was $449 now $399.99
Bose is one of the best audio names out there, and one of our favorites, and it feels great to snag a pair of its headphones for less than retail price. One of this model's standout upgrades is the revamped on-head detection, which will automatically start playback when connected to paired devices after being placed on your head. There's also the AI-powered ActiveSense ANC algorithm, which could give Sony a run for its money. Early Black Friday offers may not be as good as ones you get on the actual day, but you never know if something will be out of stock by the time the event officially kicks off. View Deal

Boombox 4: was $549.95 now $399.95
This absolute audio behemoth is my go-to Bluetooth speaker when I want something loud that still sounds superb. It delivers thumping bass while remaining beautifully clear, and is practically designed with waterproofing and a useful built-in carrying handle.View Deal

WH-1000 XM5 Headphones: was $398 now $229.99
Compared to its listing price at the time of release, a sub-$250 offer on some of the best headphones I've used isn't terrible at all. While it's still not exactly a budget-friendly option, the newer XM6 model is still on the pricier side even during early Black Friday sales. View Deal

AMBEO Soundbar Plus: was $1799.99 now $999.99
This is a our 'best splurge' option as far as soundbars go, but we were most impressed by how it can manipulate the surround-sound experience in just one device - so you won't need to spend extra on rear speakers for the full effect. There's no denying that this is a massive $800 saving, and who knows if this could drop even more as we creep closer to Black Friday. View Deal

Tablet and Chromebook deals

A big-screen tablet with 6GB RAM for under 200 bucks? The Samsung Galaxy Tab A11+ is perfect for media consumption with its 11-inch 90Hz screen, and the MediaTek MT8775 chipset offers good performance for day-to-day tasks. The modest 128GB of storage might be a limitation for those who download lots of videos or apps, but it's easy to upgrade thanks to a microSD card slot.View Deal

Lenovo Chromebook 2-in-1: was $509.99 now $329.99
This early Black Friday deal nets you a compact, lightweight 2-in-1 Chromebook at its lowest-ever Amazon price. It's got an Intel N150 processor, 4GB of RAM, and 128GB of storage – which is more than enough for smooth performance in everyday tasks. The 2-in-1 form factor makes it a good pick for watching movies on the go or scrolling the web using the touchscreen.View Deal

Lenovo Chromebook Plus i 15.3": was $399 now $349
This more powerful Chromebook Plus is a good choice if you're after a Chromebook better suited to plenty of multitasking and general productivity. It has 8GB of RAM, 128GB of SSD storage, and is powered by an Intel Core 3 CPU.View Deal

TV deals

55" U8 Series ULED Mini-LED 4K: was $1424.99 now $749.99
Just shy of $100 from its lowest price ever, the Hisense U8 series is a solid TV option if you want the complete visual and audio experience, sporting two 10W speakers in the left and right channels with a 20W subwoofer in the center. If you haven't got room for a soundbar, this makes up for it. This model also comes fitted with Google TV, so there's no need to add a streaming device on top. View Deal

Sony's Triluminos Pro display technology gives this model a vibrant and bold visual upgrade, and the audio-side of things also packs a punch with custom X-balanced speakers. As well as Dolby Atmos support, you can also access Google TV on-device, which is ideal if you're already in that smart home ecosystem. A smaller saving, yes, but it's one of our best Android TVs at a record-low price. View Deal

item.title: Is Apple cooked? The Xiaomi 18 Pro is coming for iPhone with the fastest Android chipset and a built-in back display
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Xiaomi has officially launched its latest flagship devices: the Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max
  • Both phones sport an innovative rear display and offer top-of-the-line specs
  • They're not cheap, however, with prices starting at £1,199 (roughly $1,600)

After we missed out on the Xiaomi 17 Pro and Pro Max last year, the Chinese smartphone giant is finally bringing its dual-screen flagships to the West. It's just launched the new Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, and I would be pretty worried if I were a certain Cupertino-based competitor.

Both phones look like an all-round excellent package, with top-of-the-line specs including the brand-new Snapdragon 8 Elite chipsets.

A Pro Max experience at a Pro Max price

The Xiaomi 18 Pro is the model for those after a more compact, but still powerful, phone, with its 6.4-inch 120Hz AMOLED front display and 6,000mAh battery. It's powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 chipset, paired with 12GB of RAM and either 256GB or 512GB of storage.

The Xiaomi 18 Pro Max, meanwhile, bumps the main screen size up to 6.9 inches and upgrades the chipset to the absolutely top-of-the-line Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 – currently the fastest Android SoC on the market. The base model offers 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, but there are also more expensive 12+512GB and 16+1TB versions available.

The bigger design also makes space for a much larger battery, which comes in at 7,050mAh with 100W wired HyperCharge support (the base 18 Pro, in contrast, only supports 90W wired HyperCharge).

The front displays of both phones support Xiaomi's new privacy display technology, which is effectively the company's take on Samsung's Privacy Display feature and helps obscure sensitive information from prying eyes.

Both the 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max boast similar camera setups, with a 200MP main shooter and 200MP periscope telephoto lens alongside a 50MP ultra-wide. As with other recent Xiaomi devices, the cameras were co-engineered with Leica and offer a range of photo styles inspired by the camera maker.

For me, the real highlight, however, is the innovative rear display situated on the back of both models. It offers a range of handy features, from controlling media playback to offering a real-time view of the cameras to make selfies easier.

You can fully customize it with a range of watch-like faces as well (including some options with cute 3D animal mascots) and even use generative AI to create your own apps right from the settings menu.

It's seriously cool and seems like a genuine reason to pick the 18 Pro or 18 Pro Max over other flagship models.

All of this doesn't exactly come cheap, however. The Xiaomi 18 Pro starts at £1,199 (that's roughly $1,600), and the 18 Pro Max starts at £1,399 (around $1,850) for the 12+256GB model.

They both come in four color options: Black, White, Velvet Red, and Cosmic Blue.

item.title: Xiaomi just announced a range of new accessories, including its first clip-on earbuds and a surprisingly affordable fitness band
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Xiaomi has unveiled a new line of accessories
  • It includes a new smartwatch, fitness band, and the brand's first clip-on earbuds
  • All products are available in a range of color options and can be purchased now from the Mi Store or Amazon

The arrival of the new flagship Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max might be dominating the headlines, but the Chinese smartphone giant also just lifted the curtain on a range of accessories that are worth paying attention to.

Xiaomi is getting in on the clip-on trend

If you're a fan of open-ear audio, then the new Xiaomi Clip earbuds are going to be the start of the new reveals. They're the brand's first clip-on model, and weigh just 5.5g per earbud.

If you're not familiar with this relatively recent trend, clip-on earbuds attach to your ears with a gentle clamping mechanism rather than being pushed inside your ear canal like conventional buds. This makes them highly comfortable and leaves your ear canals open to allow in background noise like traffic or conversations.

They're not a good fit for a loud commute, but such designs have become a popular choice for fitness or scenarios where you want to maintain full situational awareness while still being able to enjoy some tunes.

Xiaomi promises that the Clip earbuds will feel like they're "barely there" while in use, and accommodate a wide range of ear shapes thanks to their flexible shape-memory alloy bridge material.

Fashion is clearly a focus, and the Xiaomi Clip earbuds are offered in four distinct colorways: Sand Gold, Pearl White, Graphite Black, and Frost Purple. They all come with a compact charging case that's designed to look something like a jewelry box.

As for the more technical specs, each bud contains an 11mm dynamic driver. They offer Hi-Res certified sound and support the modern LHDC 5.0 codec. According to Xiaomi, the battery life comes in at 9 hours of music playback, with an additional 29 hours offered by the charging case.

They cost £129.99 and are available via the Mi website.

A new watch with an essential payment upgrade

There's no better companion for a new Android smartphone than a compatible smartwatch, and Xiaomi has you covered there too with the new Watch S5 41mm.

This £199.99 smartwatch boasts a 1.32 AMOLED display with up to 3,000 nits of peak brightness. It runs Xiaomi HyperOS 4 and is the first Xiaomi Watch S model compatible with Google Wallet – so you can conveniently pay with your wrist without the need for Xiaomi Pay.

It comes packed with a range of sensors, including a heart rate sensor with blood oxygen sensing capabilities, an accelerometer, gyroscope, ambient light sensor, and temperature sensor. Xiaomi also says that the watch can last up to 14 days on a single charge.

It's available in three color options: Black, Light Blue, and Ceramic White. Black and Light Blue both offer stainless steel bezels and rubber straps, while Ceramic White has a ceramic bezel and comes with a leather strap.

A new cost-conscious smart band

Finally, Xiaomi is refreshing its affordable smart band. The Xiaomi Smart Band 11 starts at just £54.99 and offers a bright 1.72-inch AMOLED display and the ability to read notifications and see call alerts, in addition to tracking your fitness.

There is a wide range of color options available, with different build materials depending on what you pick. The standard Midnight Black, Glacier Silver, Mystic Rose, and Moon Gold models feature an aluminum frame.

If you want a band with NFC capabilities, you can also pick up the crisp white ceramic edition or a full-metal unibody model in lavender.

item.title: Apple just rolled out iPhone Duo face unlock — but the Google Pixel 11 can still do so much more
item.dc:content:
What you need to know

  • Apple rolled out camera-based facial recognition for the iPhone Duo in the iOS 27.3 developer beta
  • Due to hardware limitations, you won't be able to use it for shortcuts like digital purchasing and accessing passwords
  • Though the Google Pixel 11 also packs camera-based facial ID, it's a lot more powerful

When Apple unveiled its inaugural folding phone, the iPhone Duo, it pretty much met expectations — but the biggest drawback was the company's decision to revert to Touch ID from Face ID, which felt like a huge step down for some.

However, the latest iOS 27.3 developer beta patches over this pain point, and owners of the Apple foldable can now unlock their devices with Face ID.

Well, sort of...

Face unlock, not Face ID

For the most part, the iPhone Duo's new facial recognition tool functions very similarly to the Face ID feature we all know, allowing you to unlock your device from your lock screen. But because of the foldable's limited hardware support, it's not as robust as Face ID.

Before you get excited about the iPhone Duo's new software upgrade, there are a few limitations to bear in mind. Firstly, the camera-based facial recognition tool doesn't survive on its own, and still requires the help of Touch ID. If you want to unlock your iPhone Duo using facial recognition, it requires you to have recently used Touch ID or your device's passcode within a 45-minute window, so the two go hand-in-hand.

As far as the new facial recognition tool goes, it's only available to use on the Lock Screen, and doesn't have support for features like Apple Pay, passwords, logins, and other amenities that offer the same level of convenience. Presumably because of the Duo's folding hinge, numerous displays, and overall thinness, there's no room for a TrueDepth sensor, the dedicated tool that powers Face ID and all of its capabilities.

Still, it would've been the perfect opportunity for the company to take inspiration from the likes of Google Pixel phones.

Though Google's smartphones also pack camera-based facial recognition, there's nothing that it can't do, be that making digital purchases, accessing passwords, signing into apps, and even organizing your photo gallery by the faces in each image.

That said, while Pixel phones seem to have it all, camera-based facial recognition that's not supported by a sensor lacks a layer of security, making it much easier to bypass using 2D images of a subject. With sensor-based tools, it's much more difficult to achieve this, as they analyze and create a 3D map of the face, use detection tools to pick up facial liveliness, and pack infrared scattering tools so it can scan faces in darker environments.

It's still early days, however, and users are only just getting used to a world in which Apple foldables exist. It could be that we'll have to wait until the iPhone Duo's third-gen model to see some improvements on this front — which may not arrive until 2028 at the earliest, according to Bloomberg's own Mark Gurman.

item.title: Hold on—is 'Galaxy Claw' the Samsung AI update we've been waiting on? Rumors are talking

Samsung is reportedly working on a feature called "Galaxy Claw" that wants to do everything for you—well, within reason.

Tipster AssembleDebug with Android Authority highlighted a new direction Samsung could take Galaxy AI's everyday assistance in One UI 9.5. Rumors claim to have discovered the driving force behind Galaxy Claw: the Personal Agent Core. Supposedly, this PAC will help the phone's AI "complete tasks for you by working with apps and tools" on your device.

The PAC would bring Galaxy Claw into Messages, Gmail, Contacts, and the Phone app. The tipster notes that users would have to let this AI "view and manage" much of their data in these apps. What you're getting is an AI that's active and busy when you need it to be. Task creation is a huge feature that the tipster allegedly discovered.

It seems Samsung is preparing a way for users to create a "scheduled task" that includes the task itself, frequency, and timing. The tipster's report spotted several frequency options—hourly, weekly, weekdays, and daily. What's more, they spotted an editing feature, a "run now" option, and "history." Galaxy Claw seems poised to give users more control over their personal AI experience; however, it could also affect another major feature: "Daily Brief."

Galaxy AI already features Now Brief, which keeps users on top of their priorities and offers morning round-ups of emails, news, and the like. The publication suggests Daily Brief would "summarize emails and notifications" from a user's third-party apps.

Samsung's AI is all it can think about

Let's not forget something: a similar update for Bixby was rumored not long ago. One UI 9.5 was rumored to introduce more agentic AI capabilities for Samsung's assistant, similar to what Google has done with Gemini. It was alleged that AI could better handle tasks or "actions." These actions would involve booking restaurants or appointments on the user's behalf (and per their instruction).

Some have suspected Samsung would introduce these capabilities in Bixby sometime in 2027, alongside its major One UI 9.5 update. Only time will tell if Bixby will still receive these upgrades, or if Samsung is packaging them in Galaxy AI with "Galaxy Claw."

Either way, Galaxy Claw sounds like it's dropping right into Samsung's rumored Galaxy AI subscription. Whether that makes it worth it remains up to the user. Regardless, reports suggest Samsung wants to create a Galaxy AI Premium plan for $4.99 per month or $47.99 per year. This would cover the rumored Daily Brief, Bixby Action, and Gen Video.
